title: Short Stuff: Yellow Rain
summary: Short Stuff episode on "yellow rain," the sticky yellow substance reported falling on Laos and Vietnam in the late 1970s and early 1980s, which the US accused the Soviet Union and Vietnam of using as a chemical/biological (mycotoxin, trichothecene) weapon. Covers the Hmong people's role with the French and CIA, their persecution after 1975 and refugee camps in Thailand, Secretary of State Alexander Haig's accusation, Harvard biologist Matthew Meselson's skepticism about hollowed-out pollen, and the later explanation: giant Asian honey bees defecating en masse on hot sunny days to regulate hive temperature. Also touches on Chernobyl death toll tangentially and the 2009 Thai expulsion of Hmong.

segments.title: Opening banter and yellow rain reports
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode and describe reports of sticky yellow rain falling on sunny days in Vietnam and Laos, killing plants and sickening people, especially the Hmong.

segments.title: Hmong history and US accusations
segments.summary: The Hmong fought alongside the French and then the CIA, and after the Americans withdrew around 1975 they were persecuted by the Communist government and fled to Thai refugee camps. Secretary of State Alexander Haig said the substance was a mycotoxin biological weapon, likely supplied by the Soviet Union.

segments.title: Meselson's skepticism and hollowed-out pollen
segments.summary: Harvard biologist Matthew Meselson examined samples and found hollowed-out pollen, questioned the weapon theory, noted no planes were seen, and suggested the illnesses were from dysentery and poor nutrition or moldy food.

segments.title: Honey bee feces explanation
segments.summary: Meselson proposed that giant Asian honey bees, which eat pollen's protein and excrete the hollowed shells, were the source. Researchers later found bees leave hives in large swarms on hot sunny days and defecate in flight, lowering hive temperature so larvae develop normally.

segments.title: Lingering questions, Chernobyl aside, and Hmong today
segments.summary: Hosts note the US never retracted its accusation officially, briefly discuss Chernobyl death tolls after watching the HBO series, and describe the Hmong's continued hardship, including Thailand's 2009 expulsion of thousands of Hmong.

segments.title: Sign-off and sources
segments.summary: Hosts credit the Jacob Roberts article 'The Mystery of Yellow Rain' from Distillations, the Science History Institute blog, and sign off.
